synthesis.overview:
Reality Fracture is a full-size set with ten supported two-color archetypes. The five allied 'schools' (WU surveil, UB self-mill/threshold, BR pings, RG Heartwood ramp, WG lifegain/counters) are on rails, each sharing a hybrid prepared spell. The five enemy pairs are looser shells. The glue is Empower Jace: many cards create or load a Jace token that can -1 to surveil or -3 to draw. Legendary Way enchantments give those Jaces new abilities.

Every show calls the set deep, high-powered and synergy-rich, and Lords of Limited called it an all-time great after early play. Power sits in the uncommons and rares, especially the pushed, heavily pipped gold uncommons and charms. Limited Level-Ups notes there are only 71 commons, so decks end up uncommon-heavy.

The site's simulation (800 bot decks, 100,000 games, 51.8% average drawn win rate) broadly backs the experts on red-green and on the gold removal. It is much colder on blue and on UB than the experts are. It also likes big, sturdy green and white bodies more than the reviewers do.
synthesis.speed: Early takes said fast: Limited Resources expected quick games where bounce shines. Every show that has since played it (Limited Level-Ups' rare review, Lords of Limited's #498, Martin at TCGplayer) now says slow and grindy. Games run to turn six and beyond, seven- and eight-drops get cast, and mana sinks overperform. You still need early bodies to pressure Jace tokens and protect your own. The simulation fits the grindy read. Sturdy bodies like Wrecking Gecko (56.9%) and Thalia, the Survivor (60.7%) overperform, while tempo tools lag: Unsummon 47.9%, Perfected Theory 34.0%.
consensus: Empower Jace defines the format. Attack opposing Jace tokens, and value cheap evasive or two-power creatures that can peck at them.
Red-green Heartwood ramp is real, and Craftwork Crusher and Kiora of Fire and Ashes are premium payoffs. The sim agrees: RG is the best pair at 53.2%, Kiora 61.9%, Crusher 58.7%.
The gold uncommons and charms are pushed. Twisted Fates is a near-bomb, and Konstrari Charm is the weakest charm.
Black's removal (Last Gasp, Multiply by Zero, Extended Absence, Break Under Pressure) is excellent even where black itself is rated low.
The color-hoser cycle (Flourishing Grapple, Essence Burn, Terminal Criticism, Precise Redaction, Refute Destiny) is sideboard-only in best-of-three and never maindeck in best-of-one.
Empower cards that also affect the board (Mindseeker Oculus, Hexhaven Battalion, No Admittance) beat pure Jace fuel like Protege's Awakening.
Triple-pipped gold cards like Hapatra, Twisted Fates and Mind Meanderer belong to their pair and aren't splash material.
debates: Best Way. Alex on Limited Level-Ups and Ethan on Lords of Limited say Way of the Healer. Ben on Lords says Way of the Pyromancer, which Alex graded D+ for its late-draw floor. The sim has Healer at a flat 50.3% and Pyromancer at 45.1%.
Blue's standing. Limited Level-Ups calls blue possibly the best color at common and uncommon, and Ethan has it second. The sim has blue as the weakest color, with UB last at 45.7%.
Bloombrute. Limited Resources grades it A- and LSV 4.0, while Marc on Limited Level-Ups gave it a C over thin lifegain enablers. The sim's 53.2% sits between them.

BR pings. Ben initially rated it top tier and LSV gives Stingerquill Voxmancer 3.5. Limited Level-Ups calls it the most dubious archetype, and Lords later called it fussy. The sim shows 51.0%, but on only 5% of decks.
Kiora of Salt and Sand. Luis on Limited Resources and Ethan on Lords see a real build-around. Marc on Limited Level-Ups calls the 8/8 plan a trap. The sim sides with Marc at 48.3%.
Inspired Tethermage. Ben on Lords moved it up to B- in Way decks. Limited Level-Ups (D+) and Martin at TCGplayer (1.5) are down on it. The sim shows 50.8%.
Black's rank. Both Lords hosts and Limited Level-Ups put it last. LSV calls its commons awesome, and Ethan concedes it improved in play.

colors.take: The experts are split. Limited Level-Ups called white second-worst, while Ben on Lords and Martin at TCGplayer like its depth and one-pip removal. The sim finds white's best creatures excellent: Thalia, the Survivor 60.7%, Blossom-Blessed Angel 59.5%, Lyra, Archangel of Dawn 58.5%, Ghalta the Immovable 57.3%. Yet all four white pairs land around 49-50% while being the most-drafted, so white is probably overdrafted rather than weak. Rescue Girl (46.5%) and Prophesied End (46.6%) underperform their reviews.

This is the biggest expert-sim gap. Reviewers praise blue's card flow, Countersculpt and Unsummon, and rate rares like Sphinx of False Conclusions and Seasoned Cryomancer highly. In the sim, blue pairs average under 50% and those rares sit at 46-48%. Blue's cards are skill-intensive (flash, bounce, counters), which bots handle poorly, so the truth is likely between the two. Still, don't assume blue is the best color.

The experts see black as a removal-rich support color with few threats. The sim is kinder: BR and BG are above average, Extended Absence runs 56.1% and Multiply by Zero 54.2%, and Curse-Marred Demon is a 61.1% rare. Break Under Pressure (47.0%) and UB self-mill are the soft spots.

Lords of Limited ranks red first, and everyone likes the burn (No Admittance, Violent Echoes, Fulminous Forte). The sim agrees that red is strong: every red pair except WR is above 50%, Kiora of Fire and Ashes posts 61.9%, and Pia, Determined Rebuilder 56.2%. Violent Echoes, which the shows call a mythic-level uncommon, only manages 51.0% in bot hands.

Green is the riser. Ben on Lords calls himself a green stan after playing, and Martin rates green very strong. The sim makes it the best color: RG at 53.2%, plus big commons and uncommons all posting 56-60% (Bestial Incursion, Ghalta the Unstoppable, Wrecking Gecko, Greenhouse Propagator).

pairs.experts: Surveil flyers. Limited Level-Ups calls it possibly the strongest pair, and Ben had it top tier. Lords later said it impresses but isn't premier. Signposts are Desperate Futurescribe, Fatehold Chronologist and Denzilore Fatehold.
pairs.sim: 49.1% on 14% of decks, below average. Futurescribe (57.1%) and Chronologist (54.0%) deliver. Fatehold Charm (47.5%) and Surveillance Phantasm (50.2%) do not.

pairs.experts: Luis on Limited Resources loves the Paradox Shaper self-mill loop. Lords of Limited says the mill deck hasn't impressed, and Limited Level-Ups calls the prepared mill weak.
pairs.sim: Worst pair at 45.7% (4% of decks). Paradox Shaper (41.1%) and Theorix Charm (45.0%) back the skeptics, and the sim has the better case here.

pairs.experts: Stingerquill pings. It looked scary in previews, but Limited Level-Ups calls it dubious and Lords says it collapses when the engine dies. LSV still rates Voxmancer and Grim Repriser well.
pairs.sim: 51.0%, but on only 5% of decks. That suggests it works when the lane is open, not that it's a deck to force.

pairs.experts: Heartwood ramp into Craftwork Crusher and Kiora of Fire and Ashes. Marc on Limited Level-Ups calls it the best pair, and Lords names it one of the best decks.
pairs.sim: Best pair at 53.2% on 12% of decks. Experts and sim agree.

pairs.experts: Lifegain and counters. It looks pushed, with Bloombrute and Vigorbloom Vanguard, but Limited Level-Ups warns the lifegain enablers are thinner than they look.
pairs.sim: 49.1%. Vigorbloom Vanguard and Titanbones both post 56.2%, but Vigorbloom Charm (46.5%) and Medic's Kitesail (47.2%) drag it down.

pairs.experts: Attrition and sacrifice around Twisted Fates, which Ben calls broken in half. Edgar, Ancient Bloodlord is hyped as an incredible two-drop.
pairs.sim: 49.9% on 14% of decks. Twisted Fates confirms at 57.5%, while Edgar posts just 45.1%.

pairs.experts: Spells and prowess. It is Ben's top archetype, and Limited Level-Ups advises committing to either red aggro or blue control. Clash of Elements and Saheeli, Jewel of Avishkar are the draws.
pairs.sim: 50.5% on 5% of decks, solid. Clash posts 55.9%. Tetsuko Umezawa, Pursuer posts a surprising 60.6%.

pairs.experts: Everyone doubts the deathtouch-plus-trample theme but likes Hapatra and graveyard midrange. Ben ranks it bottom tier.
pairs.sim: 50.8% on 10% of decks, better than the experts expect. Carnivorous Cultivator runs 57.8%, while Hapatra (52.1%) is merely fine.

pairs.experts: Counters aggro with Warrior's Blades and Mabel, Valley Hero. Ben rated it top tier early.
pairs.sim: The most-drafted pair (15%) at 49.5%. Warrior's Blades (51.3%) and Mabel (49.7%) are average, and aggro seems to underperform in a grindy format.

pairs.experts: The splash-the-Ways Jace deck. Ben calls it a sleeper, Marc calls Kiora's 8/8 plan a trap, and Lords later rated it slightly worse than hoped.
pairs.sim: 49.9% on 7% of decks, dead average. Mind Meanderer posts 52.9% and Kiora of Salt and Sand 48.3%.

sim_vs_experts.note: Marc on Limited Level-Ups calls it the best rare (A+), and LSV gives it 4.5. The sim has it at 48.3% over 3,315 games. Flash ambushes and loot-on-attack are exactly what bots misplay, so the experts have the better case. Still, a 4/2 body in a format full of pings and cheap removal is more fragile than an A+.
Limited Level-Ups graded it C and Limited Resources B, but it posts 60.7%. A lifelink 3/4 that taxes Ways and removal fits a slow, grindy format. The sim's case is strong, so treat it as a high pick.
Both Limited Resources and Limited Level-Ups gave it a C, while Ben on Lords called it absurdly good. It runs 59.5% over nearly 19,000 games. Ben and the sim are right; take it early.
Alex on Limited Level-Ups graded it D and Marc C-. It posts 60.6%. A 2/4 double striker is a strong body when boards stall, and the reviewers likely undersold it.

The experts rate it D+ to C- as a fringe five-drop, and Lords called it garbage. It posts 56.9% over 18,854 games. Ward 2 on a 5/5 matters in a removal-heavy, slow format. Bots may overvalue fat bodies, but it's clearly a fine playable.

Limited Level-Ups calls it one of the best commons, while the sim shows 47.9%. Bots use bounce badly, so the experts win this one. But even the shows now say multiples are unnecessary in a slow format, so don't take it over real removal.

Ben on Lords calls it the best Way and Martin gives it 4.0, but it posts 45.1%. Way of the Healer, graded A- by Alex, is also only 50.3%. Bots don't manage Jace loyalty well, so the Ways are likely better than this. Alex's worry about Pyromancer's late-game floor is real, though.

Limited Level-Ups grades it A and Martin up to 5.0 in sealed. It posts 47.5% over 2,789 games. That is a large enough sample to temper the hype: take it, but treat it as a strong card rather than a guaranteed bomb.

Limited Resources grades it B, Lords calls it incredible and LSV gives it 3.5. The sim says 45.1%. Its value comes from well-timed sacrifices that bots miss, so the experts have the edge. Still, it isn't the auto-slam two-drop the previews suggested.

Lords called it garbage in first impressions, and Ben revised it to C+ after playing. The sim puts it at 56.2% over 20,538 games. That confirms the revision: mana plus life in a slow format is worth a card slot.

advice: Lean green, and red-green above all. It's the pair both the experts and the sim like best, so take Craftwork Crusher, Kiora of Fire and Ashes and Bestial Incursion aggressively.
Draft two-drops and cheap evasive creatures that can attack Jace tokens. When attacking a Jace, send one hard-to-block creature at it and the rest at face, as Limited Level-Ups suggests.
Prioritize removal, especially Extended Absence, Multiply by Zero, No Admittance and Twisted Fates. Don't end up light on removal in a format full of strong three- to five-drops.
Don't sleep on sturdy bodies like Thalia, the Survivor, Blossom-Blessed Angel and Wrecking Gecko. The format goes long and the sim rewards them.
Avoid forcing UB self-mill or the BR ping deck. Take them only when the gold uncommons flow; Paradox Shaper and Voxmancer are weak without support.

Favor Empower Jace cards that also affect the board. Skip durdly Jace fuel like Way of the Mind Sculptor (31.7% in the sim), Way of the Cryomancer and Protege's Awakening unless you're deep in a Jace deck.
Keep color hosers in the sideboard. Flourishing Grapple wins 36.6% when drawn in the sim, which is what maindecking them looks like.
Pick up dual lands and count sources for heavy pips. Aim for 10-11 for double-blue three-drops and 12 or more for quadruple-pip cards, per Limited Level-Ups.
